## 30‑Day DBMS Study Plan **Goal:** By the end of the month you will be comfortable with core DBMS concepts, relational algebra, SQL, normalization, transaction management, and basic NoSQL ideas – enough to ace a typical undergraduate exam or certification test. --- ## How the Plan Is Structured | Phase | Days | Focus | What You’ll Do | |------|------|-------|----------------| | **Week 1** | 1‑7 | Foundations & Data Modeling | Theory, simple ER diagrams, basic SQL DDL/DML | | **Week 2** | 8‑14 | Relational Theory & Queries | Relational algebra, advanced SELECT, joins, sub‑queries | | **Week 3** | 15‑21 | Design, Normalization & Indexing | Functional dependencies, normal forms, indexing, storage | | **Week 4** | 22‑30 | Transactions, Concurrency, Recovery & Review | ACID, locking, logging, NoSQL intro, full‑scale revision, mock exam | Each day ≈ 2‑3 hours of study (adjust to your schedule). - **Lecture/Reading** – 45‑60 min - **Hands‑on practice** – 45‑60 min (SQL console, pen‑and‑paper exercises) - **Reflection/Notes** – 15‑30 min (summarise key points, write one‑sentence “cheat‑sheet” entry) --- ## WEEK 1 – Foundations & Basic SQL | Day | Topic | Sub‑topics / Activities | Practice Questions | |-----|-------|------------------------|--------------------| | **1** | Introduction to DBMS | • What is a DBMS?
• Advantages over file systems
• Three‑level architecture (internal, conceptual, external) | 1. List three advantages of using a DBMS over a flat file system.
2. Draw the three‑level architecture and label each level. | | **2** | Data Models Overview | • Hierarchical, network, relational, object‑oriented
• Why relational dominates today | 1. Match each model with its key characteristic. | | **3** | Entity‑Relationship (ER) Model – Part 1 | • Entities, attributes, primary keys
• Simple ER diagram creation | Draw an ER diagram for a **library** (books, members, loans). | | **4** | ER Model – Part 2 | • Relationships (1:1, 1:N, M:N)
• Participation & cardinality | Convert the library ER diagram into a relational schema (list tables, PK/FK). | | **5** | Relational Model Basics | • Relations, tuples, domains
• Keys (PK, FK, candidate, super) | Identify PK/FK in the schema you produced on Day 4. | | **6** | SQL DDL (Data Definition Language) | • CREATE, ALTER, DROP
• Data types, constraints (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK) | Write a CREATE TABLE statement for **Books** (ISBN PK, Title, Author, Year). | | **7** | SQL DML – INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE | • INSERT syntax, multi‑row insert
• UPDATE with WHERE, DELETE with conditions | Insert 5 sample rows into **Books**; then update the year of one book; finally delete a book with a given ISBN. | **Mini‑Revision (Day 7 Evening)** – 15 min flash‑cards: key terms, ER symbols, SQL syntax. --- ## WEEK 2 – Relational Theory & Querying | Day | Topic | Sub‑topics / Activities | Practice Questions | |-----|-------|------------------------|--------------------| | **8** | Relational Algebra – Basics | • σ (selection), π (projection), ρ (rename)
• Set operators (∪, ∩, −) | Write relational algebra for “list all book titles published after 2015”. | | **9** | Relational Algebra – Joins | • θ‑join, natural join, equi‑join, outer joins (left, right, full) | Express “books borrowed by member M101” using a natural join. | | **10** | SQL SELECT – Simple Queries | • SELECT‑FROM‑WHERE, ORDER BY, DISTINCT, LIMIT | Retrieve the top 3 most recent books. | | **11** | SQL SELECT – Aggregation | • GROUP BY, HAVING, aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX) | Find the number of books each author has written. | | **12** | SQL SELECT – Sub‑queries | • Scalar, row, column sub‑queries; EXISTS, IN, ANY/ALL | List members who have borrowed **all** books written by “Jane Austen”. | | **13** | SQL SELECT – Set Operations | • UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT (or MINUS) | Combine two queries: books published before 2000 **or** after 2020. | | **14** | Practice Day – Mixed Queries | • Solve a 5‑question worksheet covering all SELECT topics. | **Worksheet example:**
1. Find members who never borrowed a book.
2. Show authors with > 3 books, ordered by count descending.
3. … (total 5) | **Revision (Day 14 Evening)** – 10‑minute “concept map” linking relational algebra operators to their SQL equivalents. --- ## WEEK 3 – Design, Normalization & Indexing | Day | Topic | Sub‑topics / Activities | Practice Questions | |-----|-------|------------------------|--------------------| | **15** | Functional Dependencies (FDs) | • Definition, Armstrong’s axioms, closure of attribute set | Compute the closure of {A, B} given a set of FDs. | | **16** | Normal Forms – 1NF & 2NF | • Atomicity, partial dependency, decomposition | Convert a sample un‑normalized table to 1NF, then to 2NF. | | **17** | Normal Forms – 3NF & BCNF | • Transitive dependency, lossless‑join, dependency preservation | Determine if a given schema is in BCNF; if not, decompose. | | **18** | Decomposition & Anomalies | • Update, insertion, deletion anomalies; algorithmic decomposition | Identify anomalies in a sample table and propose a fix. | | **19** | Indexing Basics | • B‑tree, hash index, clustered vs non‑clustered, when to use | Given a query pattern, decide which column(s) should be indexed. | | **20** | Physical Storage & File Organization | • Heap files, sorted files, hashing, page structure, record layout | Sketch the page layout for a fixed‑length record table. | | **21** | Practice Day – Design Exercise | • End‑to‑end: start with a requirement (e.g., “online store”), draw ER, derive relational schema, identify FDs, normalize to BCNF, propose indexes. | Submit a short report (≈ 1‑page) with all steps. | **Mini‑Revision (Day 21 Evening)** – 20‑minute “cheat‑sheet” creation: list each normal form with its definition and a quick test. --- ## WEEK 4 – Transactions, Concurrency, Recovery & Review | Day | Topic | Sub‑topics / Activities | Practice Questions | |-----|-------|------------------------|--------------------| | **22** | Transaction Concepts & ACID | • Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability
• Transaction states (active, partially committed, etc.) | Explain why a bank transfer must be atomic. | | **23** | Concurrency Control – Locking | • Shared (S) vs Exclusive (X) locks, two‑phase locking (2PL) | Draw a schedule that leads to a deadlock; show how 2PL avoids it. | | **24** | Concurrency Control – Timestamp & Optimistic | • Timestamp ordering, validation phase | Given timestamps, decide commit/abort for two transactions. | | **25** | Recovery Techniques – Logging | • Write‑ahead log (WAL), log record types (undo/redo) | Sketch the log sequence for a transaction that inserts then updates a row. | | **26** | Crash Recovery & Checkpointing | • ARIES basics, checkpoint interval | Explain what happens after a crash at a checkpoint. | | **27** | Introduction to NoSQL & NewSQL | • Key‑value, document, column‑family, graph models
• CAP theorem, eventual consistency | Compare relational vs document store for a **blog** application. | | **28** | **Full‑Scale Revision Day** | • Review all cheat‑sheets, re‑solve selected problems from weeks 1‑3, identify weak spots. | Create a “one‑page summary” for each major topic. | | **29** | **Mock Exam** (2 h) | • 30 multiple‑choice + 5 short‑answer + 2 SQL coding questions (cover whole syllabus). | After finishing, grade yourself using the answer key provided below. | | **30** | **Exam Review & Reflection** | • Review mock‑exam results, revisit incorrect items, write a 200‑word reflection on what you learned and next steps. | No new questions – focus on consolidation. | --- ## DAILY TEMPLATE (for every day) 1. **Read / Watch** – 45 min (textbook chapter, lecture video, or reputable article). 2. **Take Structured Notes** – Use headings, bullet points, and a **“Key Formula/Command”** box. 3. **Hands‑On Practice** – 45 min (run SQL commands in MySQL/PostgreSQL, or solve pen‑and‑paper algebra). 4. **Self‑Quiz** – 5‑10 short questions (you can use the “Practice Questions” column). 5. **Summarise** – 5 min: write one sentence that would help you recall the day’s core idea. --- ## FINAL WEEK (Days 22‑30) – Why It Matters - **Days 22‑26** give you the *system‑level* understanding (transactions, recovery) that many exams consider “advanced” but is essential for real‑world DBAs. - **Day 27** broadens perspective to modern data stores, ensuring you can discuss trade‑offs. - **Day 28** is a *consolidation sprint*: you re‑read only your cheat‑sheets, not full chapters, which reinforces memory. - **Day 29** simulates exam conditions (time‑boxed, no notes). - **Day 30** turns the experience into a learning loop: you see gaps, fix them, and record a personal action plan (e.g., “review isolation levels next month”). --- ## QUICK REFERENCE CHEAT‑SHEET (to copy onto a single A4 page) | Category | Core Points | |----------|-------------| | **ER → Relational** | Entity → Table, PK → PK, M:N → Junction table with two FKs | | **SQL DDL** | `CREATE TABLE t (c1 INT PK, c2 VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, …);` | | **SQL DML** | `INSERT INTO t VALUES (...);`
`UPDATE t SET c1=… WHERE …;` | | **SELECT Basics** | `SELECT col1, col2 FROM t WHERE condition ORDER BY col1 DESC LIMIT 5;` | | **Aggregates** | `GROUP BY col HAVING COUNT(*)>1` | | **Joins** | `INNER JOIN` = natural/equi‑join; `LEFT OUTER JOIN` keeps left rows; `FULL OUTER JOIN` keeps both sides | | **RA ↔ SQL** | σ → `WHERE`, π → `SELECT`, ρ → `AS`, ⋈ → `JOIN` | | **Normal Forms** | 1NF: atomic values; 2NF: no partial FD on PK; 3NF: no transitive FD; BCNF: every FD X→Y, X is a superkey | | **Index Types** | B‑tree – range queries; Hash – equality; Clustered – table order; Non‑clustered – separate structure | | **ACID** | Atomicity (all‑or‑nothing), Consistency (rules preserved), Isolation (concurrent effect), Durability (persist after crash) | | **Locking** | 2PL → acquire all locks, then release; deadlock detection → wait‑‑die / wound‑‑wait | | **Logging** | Write‑Ahead Log (WAL) → log before data page write; undo/redo records | | **CAP** | Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance – can only have two at once in a distributed system | Print this sheet, keep it on your desk, and glance at it each day. --- ### 🎓 Final Tips 1. **Active Recall** – After reading, close the book and recite the definition in your own words. 2. **Spaced Repetition** – Review the cheat‑sheet on Days 14, 21, 28. 3. **Explain to Someone Else** – Teach a friend or record a 2‑minute video; teaching cements knowledge. 4. **Use Real Data** – Load a small sample (e.g., the classic “Sakila” MySQL database
